facts.fact: NITA-U's Julian Rweju said the Bank of Uganda has recently rolled out specific regulations to support and govern AI within the financial sector.
NITA-U's Julian Rweju said government is using AI on its core platforms to generate predictive reports from National ID logins on the portal and e-services, to customise services.

UGA.note: The AI uses named are on general e-services and ID, not a sector's public system.
Government is set to launch a national AI strategy before year end, but no drafting, consultation or adoption is stated.
States the country adopts off-the-shelf technology; no local AI development stated.
National ID login to the portal is mentioned only as a data source; no authentication service is described.
Nothing stated on a civil register and ID link.
Regulators rely on the Data Protection and Privacy Act for AI, but no standing, regulation or application is stated about the law.
No services portal or count of online services stated.
No enrolment count or share stated.
Nothing stated on a number at birth.
Nothing stated on who operates the ID system.
Nothing stated on registers keyed on the ID number.
AI matching of same-name citizens by biometrics is mentioned without describing the ID system's enrolment checks.
No service checking people against the national ID is described.
Nothing stated on who builds or runs government systems.
